analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md; no executable code, keys, wire protocol, or authorization logic changes. The visible changes are documentation: the head side (lines 61, 71-310) adds a GLM5Next implementation boundary section; line 61 notes that a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. The base units cover MiMo V2.6 native candidate prose (lines 832-1218), shown for context. The head unit is only the first 396 lines, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the later changed head ranges (911-919, 937, 948-968, 1239-1264, 1512-1519) were not visible and are an integration coverage limit.

Relevant threat IDs: T-041 (the SSD prefix cache), TB-007 (the inference engine) and T-028 (residual GPU memory). The /metrics note at line 61 says the refusal reason stays local. This is a documentation claim only; its code path (EngineV2SlotFactory/bridge) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. The documented behavior is that a typed refusal reason is not sent to the coordinator, which is consistent with T-041's posture of not leaking cache state. The doc also states that GLM coordinator mode uses catalog-identity chain validation (catalog entry pins version and aggregate, receipt hash, per-file manifest hashing). This supports A-004/T-012 (weight substitution) but is a documentation statement, not a verified control. The documented 'prefix-cache composes with complete-prefix store' and media exclusion from prefix lookup (line 259-260) align with T-041. The doc's statement that tool-argument routing and local /metrics expose only retained-fault state and byte counts is not a new disclosure of prompt content.

No security regression found. Next pass should check whether the later head hunks change any claims about cache scope, TTL, or encryption in T-041, and whether the doc still matches the code.
